This may only apply to some small areas perhaps around me, but I've heard people use the argument that father's should pay child custody even if they don't want to because it is in the best interest of the child, yet from what I can tell it is the concerns of the mother which come primary rather then the child. Now I'll only be talking about children once born because there's a few other issues that could come into play about any abortion talk (namely some people think conception starts life, some think it's birth, etc.).

Once born, last I knew at least, a fair number of places have 'safe haven' laws, that allow a mother to put a child into adoption anonymously, without the consent/knowledge of the father if she so chooses, and last I knew this does not work the other way around. Even if some households wouldn't be the best place to raise a child these households don't always seem to make use of these safe haven laws, in fact someone who has complete disregard for the child is less likely to put them into adoption (though still might by viewing them as an inconvenience) and given how bad the foster care system can be it may very well be in the best interest of the child to stay in a household that considers their needs then it is to be put up for adoption (though obviously not always the case, it is still a gamble while a household that does have concerns about the well-being of the child might be better then the 'average' household a child who was adopted gets, though I might be wrong about this). This also ignores when the father is not only willing but wants to raise the child even if alone. Then when it comes to a matter of child support mothers generally have to pay less if at all when the father is awarded primary custody, and they face even less social and legal pressure to pay these should they choose not to, indicating that the father has MORE responsibility over the child then a mother would (having to cover both financials and caring for the child with little if any support otherwise), furthermore when a mother receives child support, last I knew, they are under very limited if any obligation to actually spend such money on the child (beyond basic necessities even though child support is based off of an unrealistic notion of 'maintaining previous lifestyle', fact of the matter is that even if the parents didn't split but felt like having two households and bills the lifestyle would decrease as money would become tighter).

Finally, a mother can name whoever they want as the father and it gives very little legal room for a father to argue that he is not the child's biological father (in some places like France, a paternity test is illegal without the mother's consent). This is VERY against the interest of the child, not because they need to be able to find 'who their real daddy' is, but rather because knowing the biological father could become a matter of life or death as if the biological father has a deadly genetic condition that doctors are unaware about because the mother named someone else for her own benefit, and said father was unable to legally have this fact corrected, it could result in the child's death, it goes directly against the 'best interests' of the child to legally prevent the correct biological father from being listed as the biological father for medical purposes as it gambles with the child's life potentially every day.

To me this seems rather a system that for the most part puts the freedoms of the mother first followed by the best interest of the child (though some exceptions will apply when the mother can be clearly made out to be so drastically unfit that those involved cannot justify putting the invisible priority 1 ahead of the stated priority 1) followed by the freedoms of the father. This is drastically out of sync with any sort of notion of equality or even logic, the freedoms of both parents should at the very least be next to each other without instead of one being more valuable than the child with the other less, either they both should be ahead of the child or both be behind the child as they're both adults.

But those are just my thoughts, and I do apologize if I overlooked some glaring contradiction.

TL;DR- Laws and the enforcement of them appear to be concerned most with the freedoms of the mother THEN the child's best interest rather then the best interest of the child first and foremost (some exceptions will apply).
